**Visual Analysis:**

- **Plant**: Tomato
- **Affected part**: Leaves (upper and lower surfaces visible)
- **Key features observed**:
  - Pale greenish-yellow spots scattered across the upper leaf surfaces
  - Spots lack sharp/defined margins — they blend into surrounding tissue
  - Extensive chlorotic (yellow) areas across multiple leaves
  - Disease appears most severe on older/lower leaves, progressing upward
  - Small lesions visible, some coalescing into larger yellow patches
  - No obvious brown target rings (ruling out Early Blight) or water-soaked margins (ruling out Late Blight)

**Differential reasoning:**

- **Early Blight**: Would show distinct brown lesions with concentric rings and yellow halos — not visible here
- **Septoria Leaf Blotch**: Small circular lesions with gray centers and dark brown margins with pycnidia — the spots here lack those sharp borders and gray centers
- **Late Blight**: Would show purple-brown oily blotches with white cottony sporulation on undersides — not present
- **Leaf Mold**: Matches very well — pale greenish-yellow spots without definite margins on upper leaf surface, extensive chlorosis, disease progressing from lower to upper leaves, leaves withering but remaining attached

The diffuse pale yellow spots with no defined margins on the upper leaf surface, combined with the pattern of disease progression from older leaves upward, is highly characteristic of **Leaf Mold** (*Passalora fulva*).
